How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide (with code snippets) that shows you how to build and send a **RESTful GET** request to the **Cisco Nexus Dashboard** API that returns the *Device Connector Versions* information. The example uses the **6.3.1** API version and the **`get information of device connector versions`** endpoint. --- ## 1. What you’ll need | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Base URL** | `https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1` (replace with your tenant’s domain if it differs) | | **Endpoint** | `/device-connector-versions` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Authentication** | OAuth 2.0 bearer token (or API key, depending on your tenant configuration) | | **Headers** | `Authorization`, `Accept: application/json` | | **Query Parameters** | Optional filters such as `deviceId`, `connectorType`, `page`, `size`, etc. | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure about the exact query parameters, consult the *API Reference* section of the Nexus Dashboard documentation or use the “Try it out” button in the Swagger UI. --- ## 2. Build the request ### 2.1 Construct the full URL ```text https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions ``` If you want to filter by a specific device ID, append a query string: ```text https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345 ``` ### 2.2 Set the headers | Header | Value | |--------|-------| | `Authorization` | `Bearer ` | | `Accept` | `application/json` | > **Note:** Replace `` with the token you obtained via OAuth 2.0 or your API key. --- ## 3. Example code snippets Below are three common ways to send the request: ### 3.1 cURL (command line) ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### 3.2 Python (`requests` library) ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1" ENDPOINT = "/device-connector-versions" TOKEN = "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}", "Accept": "application/json", } params = { "deviceId": "12345", # optional "connectorType": "ethernet", # optional "page": 1, # optional "size": 50, # optional } response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}", headers=headers, params=params) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() print("Device Connector Versions:") for item in data.get("results", []): print(item) else: print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}") ``` > **Why use `params`?** > The `params` dictionary automatically encodes the query string for you, so you don’t have to manually concatenate it. ### 3.3 JavaScript (Node.js, `axios`) ```javascript const axios = require('axios'); const BASE_URL = 'https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1'; const ENDPOINT = '/device-connector-versions'; const TOKEN = 'YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN'; const config = { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, Accept: 'application/json', }, params: { deviceId: '12345', // optional connectorType: 'ethernet', // optional page: 1, // optional size: 50, // optional }, }; axios.get(`${BASE_URL}${ENDPOINT}`, config) .then(response => { console.log('Device Connector Versions:', response.data); }) .catch(error => { console.error('Error:', error.response ? error.response.data : error.message); }); ``` --- ## 4. Using the built‑in function (Python) If you prefer to use the helper function defined in the toolset, you can call it directly: ```python from functions import requests_get url = "https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions" params = {"deviceId": "12345"} # optional result = requests_get(url=url, params=params) print(result) ``` > **What this does** > The `requests_get` function internally performs an HTTP GET request to the supplied URL with the given query parameters. It returns the parsed JSON response (or raw text if parsing fails). --- ## 5. Common pitfalls & troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Verify that the access token is still valid and has the required scopes (`read:device-connector-versions`). | | **404 Not Found** | Double‑check the base URL and endpoint path. Make sure you’re using the correct API version (`v6.3.1`). | | **Rate limiting (429)** | Add exponential back‑off or reduce request frequency. | | **Unexpected JSON structure** | Inspect the raw response (`response.text`) to see if the API returned an error object instead of the expected data. | --- ## 6. Quick reference table | Step | Command / Code | |------|----------------| | **Build URL** | `https://api.cisco.com/nexus-dashboard/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Optional Query** | `?deviceId=12345&connectorType=ethernet&page=1&size=50` | | **cURL** | `curl -X GET "" -H "Authorization: Bearer " -H "Accept: application/json"` | | **Python** | `requests.get("", headers=..., params=...)` | | **Node.js** | `axios.get("", { headers: ..., params: ... })` | --- ### Final note Once you have the request working, you can automate it (e.g., schedule a cron job, integrate into a monitoring dashboard, or trigger alerts based on the returned data). The same pattern applies to other Nexus Dashboard endpoints—just swap the endpoint path and adjust the query parameters accordingly. Happy coding!
